# 0. Libraries

```{r libs}
# Install once if needed:
# if (!requireNamespace("BiocManager", quietly = TRUE)) install.packages("BiocManager")
# BiocManager::install(c("DESeq2", "apeglm", "vsn"))
# install.packages(c("tidyverse", "pheatmap", "RColorBrewer", "ggrepel", "GGally"))

library(DESeq2)
library(tidyverse)
library(pheatmap)
library(RColorBrewer)
library(ggrepel)
```

```{r params}
# ---- Edit these two paths ----
count_dir <- "."   # where the .converted_counts.tsv live
out_dir   <- file.path(count_dir, "DESeq2_results")        # results get written here

dir.create(out_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

# Thresholds used for calling significance / labelling volcanoes
PADJ_CUT <- 0.05
LFC_CUT  <- 1      # i.e. 2-fold
```

# 1. Build the sample sheet from the filenames

Filenames follow `CellLine_Model_Treatment_Replicate`, e.g. `A427_RMC3_Ctrl_R1`.
`model` is the cell model (parental or a drug-tolerant derivative), `treatment` is
the acute drug exposure in that experiment.

```{r sample-sheet}
files <- list.files(count_dir, pattern = "\\.converted_counts\\.tsv$", full.names = TRUE)
stopifnot(length(files) > 0)

meta <- tibble(
  file   = files,
  sample = sub("\\.converted_counts\\.tsv(\\.gz)?$", "", basename(files))
) %>%
  # split the sample name into its four components
  separate(sample,
           into   = c("cell_line", "model", "treatment", "replicate"),
           sep    = "_",
           remove = FALSE) %>%
  mutate(
    # the single factor we actually model: one level per model x treatment cell
    group  = factor(paste(model, treatment, sep = "_")),
    model  = factor(model),
    # flag parental vs drug-tolerant persister-derived line
    origin = factor(if_else(model == "Par", "Parental", "DTP"))
  ) %>%
  arrange(model, treatment, replicate) %>%
  as.data.frame()

rownames(meta) <- meta$sample
knitr::kable(meta[, c("sample", "model", "treatment", "replicate", "group")])
```

```{r sample-sheet-check}
# Sanity check: every group should have 3 replicates
table(meta$group)
```

# 2. Read the count files into a matrix

The files carry a few `##key=value` provenance lines, then a header line that
starts with `#ensid`. The reader below finds that header line rather than
hard-coding a `skip=` value, so it still works if the number of `##` lines
changes between files.

I use the **`count`** column (raw integer counts). Do **not** feed `fpkm`,
`fpkm_uq` or `tpm` into DESeq2 — it needs untransformed counts and does its own
size-factor normalisation.

```{r reader}
read_counts_file <- function(path, value_col = "count") {
  ln  <- readLines(path)                       # readLines transparently handles .gz
  hdr <- grep("^#ensid", ln)[1]                # locate the real header row
  stopifnot(!is.na(hdr))

  tab <- read.delim(
    text             = paste(ln[hdr:length(ln)], collapse = "\n"),
    header           = TRUE,
    check.names      = FALSE,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
  colnames(tab)[1] <- sub("^#", "", colnames(tab)[1])   # "#ensid" -> "ensid"
  tab[, c("ensid", "gene", "biotype", "chr", value_col)]
}

# Read everything once
count_list <- lapply(meta$file, read_counts_file)
names(count_list) <- meta$sample
```

```{r build-matrix}
# Gene annotation taken from the first file; all files should share the same rows
gene_info <- count_list[[1]][, c("ensid", "gene", "biotype", "chr")]

# Match on ensid rather than assuming identical row order across files
counts_mat <- vapply(
  count_list,
  function(x) x$count[match(gene_info$ensid, x$ensid)],
  numeric(nrow(gene_info))
)
rownames(counts_mat) <- gene_info$ensid
counts_mat <- round(counts_mat)            # DESeq2 requires integers
storage.mode(counts_mat) <- "integer"

# Guard against silent NA introduction if a file had a different gene set
stopifnot(!anyNA(counts_mat))

dim(counts_mat)
counts_mat[1:5, 1:4]
```

```{r libsize}
# Library size overview — a quick look for outlier samples
lib <- tibble(sample = colnames(counts_mat),
              total  = colSums(counts_mat)) %>%
  left_join(meta[, c("sample", "model", "treatment")], by = "sample")

ggplot(lib, aes(x = reorder(sample, total), y = total / 1e6, fill = model)) +
  geom_col() +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Assigned reads (millions)", title = "Library sizes") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 8)
```

# 3. DESeq2 object and global QC

For QC (correlation, PCA) I fit one object over all samples. The actual
statistical contrasts in section 5 are run on **subsets** of two groups at a
time — see the note there for why.

```{r dds}
stopifnot(identical(colnames(counts_mat), meta$sample))

dds_all <- DESeqDataSetFromMatrix(
  countData = counts_mat,
  colData   = meta,
  design    = ~ group
)

# Light pre-filter: keep genes with a decent count in at least a full group
keep <- rowSums(counts(dds_all) >= 10) >= 3
table(keep)
dds_all <- dds_all[keep, ]

# Variance-stabilising transform for all distance/correlation/PCA work
vsd <- vst(dds_all, blind = TRUE)
```

## 3.1 Replicate correlation heatmap

Replicates within a group should correlate noticeably better with each other
than with anything else. Spearman on VST values is fairly robust here.

```{r cor-heatmap, fig.width=11, fig.height=10}
vsd_mat  <- assay(vsd)
cor_mat  <- cor(vsd_mat, method = "spearman")

ann <- meta[, c("model", "treatment")]

pheatmap(
  cor_mat,
  annotation_col   = ann,
  annotation_row   = ann,
  clustering_distance_rows = as.dist(1 - cor_mat),
  clustering_distance_cols = as.dist(1 - cor_mat),
  col        = colorRampPalette(rev(brewer.pal(9, "Blues")))(255),
  fontsize   = 6,
  main       = "Sample-sample Spearman correlation (VST)"
)
```

```{r cor-within}
# Numeric summary: mean within-group replicate correlation, per group.
# Anything much below the rest of the table is worth investigating.
within_cor <- meta %>%
  group_split(group) %>%
  map_dfr(function(g) {
    if (nrow(g) < 2) return(NULL)
    sub <- cor_mat[g$sample, g$sample]
    tibble(group    = as.character(g$group[1]),
           mean_rho = mean(sub[lower.tri(sub)]),
           min_rho  = min(sub[lower.tri(sub)]))
  }) %>%
  arrange(mean_rho)

knitr::kable(within_cor, digits = 4)
```

## 3.2 Pairwise replicate scatter plots

Useful for eyeballing a single group in detail — swap the group name below.

```{r rep-scatter, fig.width=7, fig.height=7}
plot_replicate_pairs <- function(group_name, vmat = vsd_mat, md = meta) {
  s <- md$sample[md$group == group_name]
  stopifnot(length(s) >= 2)
  pairs(
    vmat[, s],
    pch    = ".",
    lower.panel = function(x, y, ...) {
      points(x, y, pch = ".", col = "#00000055")
      abline(0, 1, col = "red", lty = 2)
    },
    upper.panel = function(x, y, ...) {
      usr <- par("usr"); on.exit(par(usr = usr))
      par(usr = c(0, 1, 0, 1))
      text(0.5, 0.5, sprintf("r = %.3f", cor(x, y)), cex = 1.4)
    },
    main = paste("Replicates:", group_name)
  )
}

plot_replicate_pairs("Par_Ctrl")
plot_replicate_pairs("Par_RMC")
plot_replicate_pairs("RMC3_Ctrl")
plot_replicate_pairs("RMC2_RMC")
```

# 4. Helper functions: DE and volcano

```{r de-function}
#' Two-group differential expression with DESeq2
#'
#' Subsets to the two groups of interest and re-fits. This keeps dispersion
#' estimation local to the samples being compared, which matters here because
#' the panel spans several genetically distinct derivative lines — a single
#' global fit would inflate dispersion for well-behaved 3-vs-3 comparisons.
#' (If you prefer the global fit, use results(dds_all, contrast = c("group", b, a)).)
run_de <- function(group_b, group_a,
                   cts = counts_mat, md = meta,
                   min_count = 10, min_samples = 3) {

  sel <- md$sample[md$group %in% c(group_a, group_b)]
  md_s <- droplevels(md[sel, ])
  # group_a is the reference/denominator: LFC > 0 means UP in group_b
  md_s$group <- relevel(factor(md_s$group), ref = group_a)

  dds <- DESeqDataSetFromMatrix(cts[, sel], md_s, design = ~ group)
  dds <- dds[rowSums(counts(dds) >= min_count) >= min_samples, ]
  dds <- DESeq(dds, quiet = TRUE)

  # Shrink the LFCs — stops low-count genes producing huge, unstable fold changes
  cf  <- resultsNames(dds)[2]
  res <- lfcShrink(dds, coef = cf, type = "apeglm")
  raw  <- results(dds, name = cf)          # unshrunken, keeps the Wald stat
  res$stat <- raw$stat[match(rownames(res), rownames(raw))]
  
  as.data.frame(res) %>%
    rownames_to_column("ensid") %>%
    left_join(gene_info, by = "ensid") %>%
    mutate(
      contrast = paste0(group_b, "_vs_", group_a),
      sig = case_when(
        is.na(padj)                                ~ "NS",
        padj < PADJ_CUT & log2FoldChange >  LFC_CUT ~ "Up",
        padj < PADJ_CUT & log2FoldChange < -LFC_CUT ~ "Down",
        TRUE                                       ~ "NS"
      )
    ) %>%
    arrange(padj)
}
```

```{r volcano-function}
#' Volcano plot: shrunken log2FC vs -log10(adjusted p)
volcano_plot <- function(res_df, title = NULL, n_label = 20,
                         label_genes = NULL) {

  d <- res_df %>%
    filter(!is.na(padj)) %>%
    mutate(negLog10 = -log10(padj))

  # Cap infinite values (padj == 0) so the plot stays readable
  finite_max <- max(d$negLog10[is.finite(d$negLog10)], na.rm = TRUE)
  d$negLog10 <- pmin(d$negLog10, finite_max * 1.05)

  # Which genes to label: either an explicit list, or top hits per direction
  lab <- if (!is.null(label_genes)) {
    d %>% filter(gene %in% label_genes)
  } else {
    d %>% filter(sig != "NS") %>%
      group_by(sig) %>%
      slice_max(order_by = negLog10, n = n_label, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
      ungroup()
  }

  ggplot(d, aes(log2FoldChange, negLog10)) +
    geom_point(aes(colour = sig), size = 0.8, alpha = 0.6) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = c(Up = "#C0392B", Down = "#2471A3", NS = "grey75"),
                        name = NULL) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = c(-LFC_CUT, LFC_CUT), linetype = "dashed",
               colour = "grey40", linewidth = 0.3) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = -log10(PADJ_CUT), linetype = "dashed",
               colour = "grey40", linewidth = 0.3) +
    geom_text_repel(data = lab, aes(label = gene), size = 2.6,
                    max.overlaps = Inf, box.padding = 0.3,
                    segment.size = 0.2, min.segment.length = 0) +
    labs(
      title = title %||% unique(res_df$contrast),
      subtitle = sprintf("padj < %g and |log2FC| > %g:  %d up, %d down",
                         PADJ_CUT, LFC_CUT,
                         sum(res_df$sig == "Up"), sum(res_df$sig == "Down")),
      x = expression(log[2]~fold~change),
      y = expression(-log[10]~adjusted~italic(P))
    ) +
    theme_bw(base_size = 11) +
    theme(legend.position = "right",
          panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
}
```

# 5. Key comparisons: parental vs each drug-tolerant model (baseline state)

Each drug-tolerant model's untreated (`Ctrl`) samples against parental `Ctrl`.
This asks: what is constitutively rewired in the tolerant line, independent of
acute drug exposure?

```{r contrasts}
reference <- "Par_Ctrl"

dtp_ctrl_groups <- meta %>%
  filter(treatment == "Ctrl", model != "Par") %>%
  pull(group) %>% unique() %>% as.character() %>% sort()

dtp_ctrl_groups
```

```{r run-contrasts, results='hide'}
#BiocManager::install("apeglm", ask = FALSE, update = FALSE)
de_list <- setNames(
  lapply(dtp_ctrl_groups, function(g) run_de(group_b = g, group_a = reference)),
  dtp_ctrl_groups
)

# Write each result table out
invisible(lapply(names(de_list), function(g) {
  write_tsv(de_list[[g]],
            file.path(out_dir, paste0("DE_", g, "_vs_", reference, ".tsv")))
}))
```

```{r de-summary}
# How many hits per comparison
summary_tbl <- map_dfr(de_list, function(d) {
  tibble(contrast = unique(d$contrast),
         up       = sum(d$sig == "Up"),
         down     = sum(d$sig == "Down"),
         tested   = nrow(d))
})
knitr::kable(summary_tbl)
```

```{r volcanoes, fig.width=7.5, fig.height=6, results='asis'}

  cat("\n\n## ", g, " vs ", reference, "\n\n", sep = "")
```

# 6. Overlap across models

Genes changed in the same direction across several tolerant lines are more
likely to be a shared tolerance programme than a clone-specific artefact.

```{r overlap, fig.width=8, fig.height=5}
sig_long <- map_dfr(de_list, ~ filter(.x, sig != "NS")) %>%
  select(contrast, gene, ensid, log2FoldChange, padj, sig)

recurrent <- sig_long %>%
  count(gene, sig, name = "n_models") %>%
  filter(n_models >= 4) %>%
  arrange(desc(n_models))

knitr::kable(head(recurrent, 25))
write_tsv(recurrent, file.path(out_dir, "recurrent_genes_across_DTP_models.tsv"))

sig_long 

sig_long %>%
  write.csv("A427_RNAseq_output.csv")
```

```{r heatmap-recurrent, fig.width=8, fig.height=9}
# Heatmap of shrunken LFCs for the most recurrent genes
top_recurrent <- head(unique(recurrent$gene), 25)

lfc_wide <- sig_long %>%
  bind_rows(map_dfr(de_list, ~ filter(.x, gene %in% top_recurrent))) %>%
  distinct(contrast, gene, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
  filter(gene %in% top_recurrent) %>%
  select(contrast, gene, log2FoldChange) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = contrast, values_from = log2FoldChange) %>%
  column_to_rownames("gene") %>%
  as.matrix()

lfc_wide[is.na(lfc_wide)] <- 0

pheatmap(
  lfc_wide,
  color        = colorRampPalette(rev(brewer.pal(11, "RdBu")))(255),
  breaks       = seq(-4, 4, length.out = 256),
  fontsize_row = 6,
  fontsize_col = 8,
  main         = "log2FC vs parental control, recurrently changed genes"
)
```
```{r}
#replicates - heatmap
top_recurrent <- head(unique(recurrent$gene), 25)

# Map symbols back to ensid (VST matrix is keyed on ensid)
ids <- gene_info %>%
  filter(gene %in% top_recurrent, ensid %in% rownames(vsd_mat)) %>%
  distinct(gene, .keep_all = TRUE)        # drop duplicate symbols

# Show the untreated samples only — that's what the contrasts compared
samps <- meta$sample[meta$treatment == "Ctrl"]
samps <- samps[order(meta[samps, "model"] != "Par",   # parental block first
                     meta[samps, "model"],
                     meta[samps, "replicate"])]

expr <- vsd_mat[ids$ensid, samps, drop = FALSE]
rownames(expr) <- ids$gene

# Centre each gene on the mean of the parental control replicates,
# so values are log2 difference from parental — comparable to the LFC version
par_samples <- meta$sample[meta$group == "Par_Ctrl"]
expr_c <- expr - rowMeans(expr[, par_samples, drop = FALSE])

ann_col <- meta[samps, c("model", "treatment"), drop = FALSE]

pheatmap(
  expr_c,
  color            = colorRampPalette(rev(brewer.pal(11, "RdBu")))(255),
  breaks           = seq(-4, 4, length.out = 256),
  annotation_col   = ann_col,
  cluster_cols     = FALSE,                       # keep replicates grouped
  gaps_col         = cumsum(table(droplevels(meta[samps, "model"]))),
  show_colnames    = TRUE,
  fontsize_row     = 7,
  fontsize_col     = 7,
  main             = "VST expression vs parental control mean, per replicate"
)
```

```{r}
# Rank within each direction: recurrence first, effect size as tiebreak
recurrent_dir <- sig_long %>%
  group_by(gene, sig) %>%
  summarise(n_models = n(), mean_lfc = mean(log2FoldChange), .groups = "drop")

top_up <- recurrent_dir %>%
  filter(sig == "Up") %>%
  arrange(desc(n_models), desc(mean_lfc)) %>%
  slice_head(n = 5)

top_up

top_dn <- recurrent_dir %>%
  filter(sig == "Down") %>%
  arrange(desc(n_models), mean_lfc) %>%
  slice_head(n = 5)

sel <- c(top_up$gene, top_dn$gene)      # up block first, then down block

# Map symbols to ensid, then restore the up/down ordering
ids <- gene_info %>%
  filter(gene %in% sel, ensid %in% rownames(vsd_mat)) %>%
  distinct(gene, .keep_all = TRUE)
ids <- ids[match(sel, ids$gene), ]
ids <- ids[!is.na(ids$ensid), ]         # drop any lost to the VST pre-filter

samps <- meta$sample[meta$treatment == "Ctrl"]
samps <- samps[order(meta[samps, "model"] != "Par",
                     meta[samps, "model"],
                     meta[samps, "replicate"])]

expr <- vsd_mat[ids$ensid, samps, drop = FALSE]
rownames(expr) <- ids$gene

par_samples <- meta$sample[meta$group == "Par_Ctrl"]
expr_c <- expr - rowMeans(expr[, par_samples, drop = FALSE])

ann_col <- meta[samps, c("model", "treatment"), drop = FALSE]

# Row gap sits after however many "up" genes actually survived the mapping
n_up <- sum(ids$gene %in% top_up$gene)

pheatmap(
  expr_c,
  color            = colorRampPalette(rev(brewer.pal(11, "RdBu")))(255),
  breaks           = seq(-4, 4, length.out = 256),
  annotation_col   = ann_col,
  cluster_cols     = FALSE,
  cluster_rows     = FALSE,              # keep the up/down grouping
  gaps_col         = cumsum(table(droplevels(meta[samps, "model"]))),
  gaps_row         = n_up,
  show_colnames    = TRUE,
  fontsize_row     = 8,
  fontsize_col     = 8,
  main             = "Top 5 up / top 5 down vs parental control"
)
```

# 9. GSEA: drug-tolerant models vs parental

Gene set enrichment on the same contrasts as section 5. GSEA uses the **whole
ranked list**, not a filtered significant set — that is what distinguishes it
from over-representation analysis and why it can detect coordinated shifts in a
pathway where no single gene passes padj.

```{r gsea-libs}
 #BiocManager::install(c("fgsea"))
 #install.packages("msigdbr")
library(fgsea)
library(msigdbr)
```

## 9.1 Gene sets

`msigdbr` ships the MSigDB data inside the package, so this works on a cluster
node with no internet.

```{r gsea-sets}
# msigdbr renamed its arguments/columns at v10 (category -> collection,
# gs_cat -> gs_collection). This pulls everything once and adapts either way.
msig <- msigdbr(species = "Homo sapiens")

cat_col <- if ("gs_collection" %in% names(msig)) "gs_collection" else "gs_cat"
sub_col <- if ("gs_subcollection" %in% names(msig)) "gs_subcollection" else "gs_subcat"

make_pathways <- function(collection, subcollection = NULL) {
  d <- msig[msig[[cat_col]] == collection, ]
  if (!is.null(subcollection)) d <- d[d[[sub_col]] == subcollection, ]
  split(d$gene_symbol, d$gs_name)
}

# Hallmark: 50 well-curated sets, the sensible default for a first pass
pw_hallmark <- make_pathways("H")

# Optional extras — Reactome is broader but noisier, C6 is oncogenic signatures
pw_reactome <- make_pathways("C2", "CP:REACTOME")
pw_onco     <- make_pathways("C6")

length(pw_hallmark)
```

## 9.2 Building the ranked list

The metric determines what GSEA sees. Options, in rough order of preference:

- `stat` — the Wald statistic. Combines effect size and precision in one number.
  Best default.
- `signed_p` — `sign(log2FC) * -log10(pvalue)`. Use if `stat` isn't available.
  Behaves similarly but saturates when p-values hit the floor.
- `lfc` — shrunken log2 fold change. Effect-size driven, ignores how well
  each gene was measured. Reasonable, but noisier sets can dominate.

Never rank by unshrunken raw fold change — low-count genes with wild ratios end
up at both extremes of the list, which is exactly where GSEA weights hardest.

```{r gsea-ranks}
build_ranks <- function(res_df, metric = c("stat", "signed_p", "lfc")) {
  metric <- match.arg(metric)

  d <- res_df %>%
    filter(!is.na(gene), gene != "", !is.na(pvalue))

  d$score <- switch(metric,
    stat     = d$stat,
    signed_p = sign(d$log2FoldChange) * -log10(d$pvalue),
    lfc      = d$log2FoldChange
  )

  d <- d %>% filter(is.finite(score))

  # Duplicate gene symbols (several ensids per symbol) must be collapsed —
  # fgsea needs a named vector with unique names. Keep the strongest signal.
  d <- d %>%
    group_by(gene) %>%
    slice_max(order_by = abs(score), n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
    ungroup()

  setNames(d$score, d$gene) %>% sort(decreasing = TRUE)
}

# Check the metric exists before relying on it
if (!"stat" %in% names(de_list[[1]])) {
  warning("No 'stat' column - see the run_de edit, or use metric = 'signed_p'")
}

ranks_list <- lapply(de_list, build_ranks, metric = "stat")

# Sanity check on one contrast
head(ranks_list[[1]], 5)
tail(ranks_list[[1]], 5)
length(ranks_list[[1]])
```

## 9.3 Run fgsea across all models

```{r gsea-run}
run_gsea <- function(ranks, pathways, label, min_size = 15, max_size = 500) {
  set.seed(42)                       # fgsea is stochastic; fix for reproducibility
  fgsea(
    pathways = pathways,
    stats    = ranks,
    minSize  = min_size,
    maxSize  = max_size,
    eps      = 0                     # allow p-values below the default floor
  ) %>%
    as_tibble() %>%
    mutate(contrast = label) %>%
    arrange(padj)
}

gsea_list <- imap(ranks_list, ~ run_gsea(.x, pw_hallmark, .y))

# leadingEdge is a list column - flatten before writing to disk
write_gsea <- function(g, file) {
  g %>%
    mutate(leadingEdge = map_chr(leadingEdge, paste, collapse = ",")) %>%
    write_tsv(file)
}

invisible(imap(gsea_list, ~ write_gsea(
  .x, file.path(out_dir, paste0("GSEA_hallmark_", .y, "_vs_", reference, ".tsv"))
)))

# Top sets for one model
gsea_list[[1]] %>%
  select(pathway, NES, pval, padj, size) %>%
  head(15) %>%
  knitr::kable(digits = 4)
```

## 9.4 NES across all models

The useful view: which pathways move in the same direction across independent
tolerant lines. A set enriched in one clone could be clonal drift; one enriched
in five is a programme.

```{r gsea-heatmap, fig.width=9, fig.height=10}
gsea_all <- bind_rows(gsea_list)

# Keep sets significant in at least two models, to cut the matrix down
keep_sets <- gsea_all %>%
  filter(padj < 0.05) %>%
  count(pathway) %>%
  filter(n >= 2) %>%
  pull(pathway)

nes_mat <- gsea_all %>%
  filter(pathway %in% keep_sets) %>%
  mutate(pathway = str_remove(pathway, "^HALLMARK_") %>% str_replace_all("_", " ")) %>%
  select(pathway, contrast, NES) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = contrast, values_from = NES) %>%
  column_to_rownames("pathway") %>%
  as.matrix()

nes_mat[is.na(nes_mat)] <- 0        # not tested / filtered out

# Star the cells that were individually significant
star_mat <- gsea_all %>%
  filter(pathway %in% keep_sets) %>%
  mutate(pathway = str_remove(pathway, "^HALLMARK_") %>% str_replace_all("_", " "),
         lab = if_else(!is.na(padj) & padj < 0.05, "*", "")) %>%
  select(pathway, contrast, lab) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = contrast, values_from = lab) %>%
  column_to_rownames("pathway") %>%
  as.matrix()
star_mat[is.na(star_mat)] <- ""
star_mat <- star_mat[rownames(nes_mat), colnames(nes_mat), drop = FALSE]

pheatmap(
  nes_mat,
  display_numbers = star_mat,
  number_color    = "black",
  color           = colorRampPalette(rev(brewer.pal(11, "RdBu")))(255),
  breaks          = seq(-3, 3, length.out = 256),
  fontsize_row    = 8,
  fontsize_col    = 9,
  main            = "Hallmark NES vs parental control  (* padj < 0.05)"
)
```

## 9.5 Barplot for a single model

```{r gsea-bar, fig.width=8, fig.height=6}
plot_gsea_bar <- function(g, n = 15, padj_cut = 0.05) {
  d <- g %>%
    filter(padj < padj_cut) %>%
    slice_max(abs(NES), n = n, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
    mutate(pathway = str_remove(pathway, "^HALLMARK_") %>% str_replace_all("_", " "),
           dir = if_else(NES > 0, "Up in model", "Down in model"))

  ggplot(d, aes(x = NES, y = reorder(pathway, NES), fill = dir)) +
    geom_col() +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c("Up in model" = "#C0392B",
                                 "Down in model" = "#2471A3"), name = NULL) +
    labs(x = "Normalised enrichment score", y = NULL,
         title = paste("Hallmark GSEA:", unique(g$contrast))) +
    theme_bw(base_size = 10)
}

plot_gsea_bar(gsea_list[["RMC3_Ctrl"]])
```

## 9.6 Enrichment plot for one pathway

The classic running-score curve. Useful for checking whether a hit is driven by
a coherent block of genes or by a handful at one extreme.

```{r gsea-enrich, fig.width=7, fig.height=4}
plotEnrichment(
  pw_hallmark[["HALLMARK_EPITHELIAL_MESENCHYMAL_TRANSITION"]],
  ranks_list[["RMC3_Ctrl"]]
) +
  labs(title = "EMT hallmark, RMC3 vs parental")
```

## 9.7 Leading edge genes

The subset actually driving each enrichment — the sensible starting point for
picking candidates to validate.

```{r gsea-leading}
gsea_all %>%
  filter(padj < 0.05) %>%
  slice_max(abs(NES), n = 5) %>%
  transmute(contrast, pathway,
            NES = round(NES, 2), padj = signif(padj, 3),
            leading_edge = map_chr(leadingEdge, ~ paste(head(.x, 12), collapse = ", "))) %>%
  knitr::kable()
```
